clue.text: Pig had trapped tail

indicators.note: the pig holds the next word inside it, as an animal trapped in a pen

parts.note: a sow is a female pig
taken as written

explanation.surface: A pig has caught its own tail, or some other animal's, in a trap.
explanation.walkthrough: 'tail' looks like a noun belonging to the pig, but it is a verb: to follow someone closely.
explanation.definitionFit: Both verbs mean to follow someone secretly, as a detective trails a suspect.

clue.text: Reluctantly accepts criterion that summer has arrived?

definitions.meaning: to put up with an insult or a bitter pill
migrating birds whose return signals summer, though 'one doesn't make a summer'

explanation.definitionFit: The verb means grudgingly put up with; the birds are the traditional sign of summer's arrival.

clue.text: Bill supported by clergyman is correct

indicators.note: in a down clue the second piece sits underneath the first, holding it up

parts.note: AC is short for account, a bill
a curate is an assistant parish priest

explanation.surface: A bill backed by a churchman is right.
explanation.definitionFit: Accurate and correct are synonyms meaning free from error.

clue.text: They enable backward-looking people to progress

definitions.text: They enable backward-looking people to progress

parts.words: They enable backward-looking people to progress
parts.note: rowers face the stern, looking backwards, while the blades drive the boat forwards

explanation.surface: Something that helps reactionaries move forward.
explanation.walkthrough: 'backward-looking' suggests old-fashioned people; literally it is rowers facing the wrong way.
explanation.definitionFit: Rowing blades propel a boat whose crew sit facing backwards.

clue.text: Soccer player gets the bird for impudent retorts

parts.note: a back is a defender in football
a chat is a small songbird such as the stonechat

explanation.surface: A footballer is booed or given the finger for answering back cheekily.
explanation.walkthrough: 'gets the bird' suggests being jeered, but the bird here is simply the chat.
explanation.definitionFit: Cheeky answering back to someone in authority is the standard sense of the noun.

clue.text: E.g. for example?

parts.note: the letters e.g. are a shortened form of the Latin for 'for example'

explanation.surface: Reads as a definition quoting an instance.
explanation.walkthrough: 'E.g.' seems to introduce an example; in fact e.g. is itself the example of the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: A shortened form of a word or phrase, like e.g. for exempli gratia.

clue.text: Toy that needs a wind to get going

definitions.text: Toy that needs a wind to get going

parts.words: Toy that needs a wind to get going
parts.note: a flying toy needs a breeze, not winding up like clockwork

explanation.surface: A clockwork toy that must be wound up before it moves.
explanation.walkthrough: 'wind' reads as winding a key; it is the breeze.
explanation.definitionFit: A paper or fabric flier on a string is lifted only by moving air.

clue.text: Possibly Hudson Bay may have come from one of these

definitions.text: Bay may have come from one of these

indicators.note: suggests the name may be rearranged into another form

explanation.surface: A trivia line about where Canada's Hudson Bay got its name.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Bay' looks like the body of water; it is the deep howl a hunting dog gives.
explanation.definitionFit: Hunting dogs bay, or howl, so a bay is the sound made by one.

clue.text: He'd ten unusual words to finish a book

indicators.note: an unusual arrangement of these letters gives something new

parts.note: the letters H, E and D as printed

explanation.surface: An author with ten odd words to close a novel.
explanation.definitionFit: The traditional closing phrase printed on a story's final page.

clue.text: Current binder for correspondence

parts.note: AC is alternating current
a cord ties or binds things together

explanation.surface: An electrical cable or string offered as something to hold letters together.
explanation.walkthrough: 'correspondence' suggests letters, but it means agreement or matching.
explanation.definitionFit: Correspondence in the sense of agreement or harmony between things is a synonym.

clue.text: Hard to fathom corruption engulfing good man and king

indicators.note: the word for corruption swallows up the following pieces, surrounding them

parts.note: abuse, as in abuse of office, is corruption
ST, saint, is the crossword good man
R is rex, king

explanation.surface: A scandal of corruption that swallows up a virtuous man and a monarch is baffling.
explanation.walkthrough: 'engulfing' tells us the saint and king are swallowed by the corruption word, landing after its second letter.
explanation.definitionFit: Something obscure and difficult to understand is described by this adjective.

clue.text: Not allowed to succeed?

parts.note: succeed in the sense of follow as heir, not achieve success

explanation.surface: Someone barred from making a success of things.
explanation.walkthrough: 'succeed' reads as do well; it means inherit.
explanation.definitionFit: A child cut out of a will is barred from succeeding to an estate.

clue.text: Induce the French to go round ancient city

indicators.note: the French article surrounds the city name, going round it

parts.note: le is French for the
Ur was a city of ancient Mesopotamia

explanation.surface: Persuading the French to tour an ancient city.
explanation.definitionFit: To entice or tempt someone into doing something is a synonym of induce.

clue.text: Clergyman inwardly pious? The reverse — a treacherous type

indicators.note: the clue tells us to turn the clergyman's title round backwards
the word for pious is placed within the clergyman piece

parts.note: Rev, Reverend, is a clergyman's title
PI is a common short form of pious

explanation.surface: A cleric who seems devout within proves the opposite: a traitor.
explanation.walkthrough: 'inwardly' puts the pious letters inside the clergyman's title, giving REPIV; 'The reverse' then turns the whole of that back to front, not just one piece.
explanation.definitionFit: The snake is a byword for a treacherous, spiteful person.

clue.text: Party back in power for old Scandinavia

indicators.note: the party word is read backwards

parts.note: a do is a party

explanation.surface: A political party returning to government in old Scandinavia.
explanation.definitionFit: The chief Norse god was the highest divine power worshipped in pre-Christian Scandinavia.

clue.text: Cornish city organised tour crossing river

indicators.note: the reworked letters span the river letter, enclosing it
the letters of the word are rearranged in a new order

explanation.surface: A planned tour crossing a river in a Cornish city.
explanation.walkthrough: 'organised' makes TRUO, which goes round R.
explanation.definitionFit: This is the only city in Cornwall, the county at England's south-western tip.

clue.text: Holy city came about, within century

indicators.note: the century letter goes within the reworked letters
the letters are turned about into another order

parts.note: C is the Roman numeral for a hundred

explanation.surface: A sacred city came into being within a hundred years.
explanation.definitionFit: The birthplace of Muhammad is the holiest city of Islam.

clue.text: You may be well-advised to act on his spot judgment

definitions.text: You may be well-advised to act on his spot judgment

parts.words: You may be well-advised to act on his spot judgment
parts.note: a dowser picks the spot where a well should be dug, so his advice is literally about wells

explanation.surface: Praise for someone whose snap decisions are worth following.
explanation.walkthrough: 'well-advised' and 'spot judgment' read as sound quick decisions; really they are advice on where to sink a well.
explanation.definitionFit: A dowser searches for underground water with a rod and chooses the spot to dig a well.

clue.text: County relatives will supply leather

parts.note: Bucks is short for Buckinghamshire, an English county
kin are relatives

explanation.surface: Family in the shires will provide hides.
explanation.definitionFit: Soft leather made from deer or sheep hide is a kind of leather.

clue.text: Armaments open war clashes before end of July

indicators.note: the reworked letters come ahead of the final piece
the words clash and jumble into a new order
takes the last letter of the word

explanation.surface: Weapons cause open conflict to break out before late July.
explanation.definitionFit: Weapons collectively make up armaments, a synonym.

clue.text: Thrice curate in turn, a constructive way to make a living

definitions.text: a constructive way to make a living

indicators.note: the letters are turned about into a new order

explanation.surface: A curate serving three times over, by turns, as a worthwhile career.
explanation.definitionFit: Designing buildings is a profession whose work is literally constructive.

clue.text: Ring to summon for service

definitions.meaning: to order into the armed forces

explanation.definitionFit: The phrasal verb means both telephone and conscript into military service.

clue.text: Boris strangely takes a pressurised line

indicators.note: the jumbled name takes in the article, holding it inside
the name is strangely jumbled into a different order

explanation.surface: Boris oddly adopts a hard line under pressure.
explanation.walkthrough: 'strangely' makes ISOBR, with A taken in.
explanation.definitionFit: A weather-map line joining points of equal atmospheric pressure.

clue.text: A London orchestra as well

parts.note: LSO is the London Symphony Orchestra

explanation.surface: A London orchestra performing too.
explanation.definitionFit: The adverb means in addition or too, a plain synonym.

clue.text: Previous head of a religious body

definitions.meaning: the superior of a priory or the deputy in an abbey of monks

explanation.definitionFit: One word is both an adjective meaning earlier and the title of a monastic superior.

clue.text: Leave out large container

definitions.meaning: a big open bin for rubbish, a British term for a dumpster

explanation.definitionFit: The verb means omit, and the British noun is a large builder's rubbish bin.

clue.text: Word or sentence

definitions.meaning: an expression, as in a technical word
a period of imprisonment, as in a jail sentence

explanation.definitionFit: The noun means both an expression and a fixed period, such as a prison stretch.

clue.text: Collectively neither one thing nor the other

definitions.text: Collectively neither one thing nor the other

parts.words: Collectively neither one thing nor the other
parts.note: it is not one or the other alone, but the two taken together

explanation.surface: Something taken together is ambiguous, neither one thing nor the other.
explanation.walkthrough: The idiom suggests indecision; read literally it means the pair together.
explanation.definitionFit: The word refers to two things together, not either individually.

clue.text: One-time party animal backing words to music

parts.note: Lib, the Liberals, a former British political party

indicators.note: the animal's name is turned back to front

parts.note: the otter is a river animal

explanation.surface: A former partygoer, now a wild creature, supporting the lyrics to a song.
explanation.walkthrough: 'backing' turns OTTER into RETTO; the Liberal Party merged into the Liberal Democrats in 1988.
explanation.definitionFit: The text of an opera or musical is set to its score.

clue.text: Such a means to an end barely contemplated by Hamlet

definitions.text: Such a means to an end barely contemplated by Hamlet

parts.words: Such a means to an end barely contemplated by Hamlet
parts.note: in the 'To be or not to be' speech Hamlet muses on ending his life 'with a bare ...'

explanation.surface: Hamlet hardly considered this way of finishing things.
explanation.walkthrough: 'barely' seems to mean hardly; it points to Shakespeare's phrase 'a bare' dagger.
explanation.definitionFit: Here the word means a small dagger, the weapon Hamlet imagines for suicide.

clue.text: PM's diary set out high points of Egyptian tour

indicators.note: the letters are laid out afresh in a new arrangement

parts.note: the letters P, M and S as printed

explanation.surface: The Prime Minister's schedule lays out the highlights of a visit to Egypt.
explanation.definitionFit: The great tombs at Giza are the literal high points of any Egyptian trip.

clue.text: Retiring worker's seen in humble dwelling

indicators.note: the worker is placed within the word for retiring

parts.note: retiring means shy, reserved
an ant is the crossword worker

explanation.surface: A pensioned-off labourer living in a modest home.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Retiring' suggests leaving work, but it means shy.
explanation.definitionFit: A shack or crude hut is a poor, humble home.
